tagline: A short road up to a park the CCC built.
intro: Douthat State Park Road leaves Interstate 64 at Cliftondale Park for Douthat State Park, in the Allegheny Mountains, and beyond the park carries on over to Route 39 near Bath Alum.

The park is one of Virginia's six originals, opened on June 15, 1936. About 600 men of the Civilian Conservation Corps built most of it between 1933 and 1942, one company on forestry and trails, one on the office, shelters and first 25 cabins, one on the dam. For its first 29 years state law kept non-white visitors out, and the Clifton Forge NAACP pressed for Green Pastures Recreation Area instead, which opened in 1940.

moments.title: Longdale
moments.text: A hamlet near the North Mountain line of the Chesapeake and Ohio, where a station of the same name stood in the nineteenth century and a road called Longdale Station still runs.

moments.title: Douthat Lake
moments.text: CCC Company 1373 dammed Wilson Creek, the only natural body of water in the area, to make the 50-acre lake, and the creek still runs down out of the mountains into it.
